learning_outcomes.text: Enable the future 'Mechanics' engineer to understand, implement, use, interpret, and improve the tools and techniques used in measurements and controls.

Favor the choice and development of control techniques by integrating notions of cost, reliability, compatibility with quality imperatives, and the capacity of those who will implement these techniques. For certain techniques, emphasis will be placed on safety conditions related to their implementation.
The engineer must not only be able to perform the control or measurement, but above all to interpret the results and choose the location and method of physically measured information.
Practical work will consist of discipline-specific practical work and applications to all measurement practical work in other scientific and technical disciplines.
Contribute to the training of engineers who master digital tools of information and communication technologies to address problems in several application sectors.

syllabus_topics: Physical principle of mechanical, pneumatic, electrical, opto-electronic sensors and their conditioning.
Metrological characteristics of sensors: exactitude, sensitivity, operating ranges, drifts and external constraints, bandwidth, response time.
Measurement processing: amplification, data transmission, analog processing (filtering...).
Signal processing: sampling, temporal descriptors, frequency descriptors, spectral analysis.
Application elements: dimensional metrology, process control sensors, data acquisition and processing software, sensor selection.
Knowledge control: 2 written assignments + 2 practical works.
degree: Diplôme d'ingénieur Centrale Nantes, spécialité Mécanique (apprentissage)
